messages:
rachael: ACME production reporting a sudden p95/p99 latency regression starting ~13:02 UTC. Symptoms: long queue wait, increased 429s, and a handful of 500 auth errors. Customer trace: request_id=acme-req-9a3f, wait_ms=11850, service_time_ms=30. Can we triage?

acmeops: Yep seeing it on our side — interactive docs call slower, sometimes times out. No code changes on our side.

tom: Can you paste a minimal repro curl and the full log lines? Also which model/route? Sounds like admission control kicked in.

rachael: Repro:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \n -d '{"model":"gpt-lite-3","input":"hello"}'
```
Log snippet from proxy: `tenant=acme wait_ms=11850 queued=42 inflight=85 max_inflight=100 admission=throttled auth_err=3 billing_err=1`

mike: Looking at infra graphs — worker CPU fine, but request_queue depth for acme spiked at 13:01 and sustained for ~6m. Inflight peaked near tenant concurrency cap. Also saw auth-db latency spikes correlated at same time. Possible combo: auth timeouts causing workers to hold requests longer which increases queueing and then admission rejects.

eng-oncall: Agreed. If auth DB has intermittent spikes, requests block while waiting for token validation, that inflates queue and triggers admission. Two immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily increase tenant concurrency cap for acme; 2) enable waitlist/degraded-fallback for their route so we drop to smaller model or fast-fail rather than piling up.

rachael: ACME asks for quick fix — they need production traffic steady. Can we do a short hotfix?

mike: I'll do a 30m bump to concurrency and enable fallback to gpt-small for that tenant. Command:
```
# increase tenant concurrency (temporary)
redwoodctl tenants update acme --concurrency 250 --expire 30m
# enable route fallback
redwoodctl routes update acme.default --fallback-model gpt-small --fallback-rate 0.3
```
Doing now.

deploy-bot: change accepted, applying to control plane.

billing-bot: Note: there were ~6 `billing:invalid_account` responses at 13:03 for same tenant. Might be unrelated, but could have caused retries on client side.

tom: Important: if client retries on billing/auth transient errors without jitter/backoff, that'll amplify queueing. We should ask customer to check retry behaviour.

rachael: ACME confirms they had a short retry storm from their SDK (no backoff). They're patching.

mike: Monitoring — queue depth dropping, p95 back to normal, p99 tail improving. Auth error count trending down. Keep watch for next 20m.

eng-oncall: Follow-up actions:
- (mike) investigate auth-db query latency root cause and correlate with DB team logs — owner: mike, ETA 24h
- (tom) add an automated guard to detect when auth lat spikes and proactively enable tenant fallback for heavy tenants — owner: tom, ETA 3d
- (rachael) ask ACME to implement jittered exponential backoff in SDK and confirm deploy — owner: rachael, ETA 2h
- (billing-bot) billing errors owner to triage separately and confirm not the root cause — owner: billing team, ETA 8h

rachael: Thanks all — customer updated that UX is back to normal. I'll close after we verify the auth-db root cause. :thumbsup:

acmeops: Thanks, appreciate the fast turn.

mike: One more note: recorded `wait_ms` metric spike around that window. We'll add a short-lived alert for tenant wait_ms > 5s for >2m to catch similar issues earlier.

eng-oncall: Filing follow-up ticket: INF-7453 "auth-db intermittency leading to tenant queueing and admission". Will include traces and mitigation runbook.

rachael: Closing loop with ACME in 30m once we confirm stability.
